review_locator: PMCID:PMC6028070, Negative Regulation of Cytokine Signaling in Immunity; PMCID:PMC3714205, SOCS proteins in development and disease
primary_title: A novel cytokine-inducible gene CIS encodes an SH2-containing protein that binds to tyrosine-phosphorylated interleukin 3 and erythropoietin receptors
decision_basis: The review-guided primary identifies CISH/CIS as an immediate-early IL-3-inducible gene in hematopoietic cells and links its induction to the cytokine-receptor signaling region; CISH then associates with phosphorylated cytokine receptors as negative feedback.
limitations_preserved: Preserve CISH as an IL-3-associated negative-feedback gene output and distinguish its later receptor association from the gene-expression edge; no universal STAT5 promoter mechanism, terminal-TF inference or SCI relevance

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6363037, Myeloid cell leukemia 1 (MCL-1), an unexpected modulator of protein kinase signaling during invasion; PMCID:PMC5652725, Targeting signaling and apoptotic pathways involved in chemotherapeutic drug-resistance of hematopoietic cells
primary_title: Interleukin-3 Stimulation of mcl-1 Gene Transcription Involves Activation of the PU.1 Transcription Factor through a p38 Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase-Dependent Pathway
decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows IL-3 induces MCL1 transcription and Mcl-1 mRNA/protein in Ba/F3 cells through PI3K/Akt and a p38-PU.1-dependent promoter pathway, with pathway inhibition reducing the output and survival.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the Ba/F3, p38-PU.1 and PI3K/Akt pathway context; this is an output bridge rather than proof of a direct IL-3-to-MCL1 promoter contact or universal survival mechanism

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7605919, GM-CSF: A Promising Target in Inflammation and Autoimmunity; PMCID:PMC4370199, Pivotal Roles of GM-CSF in Autoimmunity and Inflammation
primary_title: The transcription factors STAT5A/B regulate GM-CSF-mediated granulopoiesis
decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows GM-CSF induces BCL2L1/Bcl-xL in granulocyte-macrophage progenitors and that this response is lost in hematopoietic Stat5a/b-null cells, linking the survival-gene output to a STAT5-dependent GM-CSF branch.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the GM-CSF/STAT5A-B context and granulocyte-lineage model; transcriptome/Stat5-null evidence supports an associated output bridge, not universal direct promoter occupancy, cytokine exclusivity or SCI relevance

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7605919, GM-CSF: A Promising Target in Inflammation and Autoimmunity; PMCID:PMC4370199, Pivotal Roles of GM-CSF in Autoimmunity and Inflammation
primary_title: The transcription factors STAT5A/B regulate GM-CSF-mediated granulopoiesis
decision_basis: The review-guided primary identifies CFLAR as a GM-CSF-induced survival/proliferation gene in granulocyte-macrophage progenitors whose induction is absent in Stat5a/b-null hematopoietic cells.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the granulocyte-progenitor and STAT5A/B-null comparison; CFLAR is a transcriptome-supported output and not a direct receptor-to-gene biochemical interaction or SCI-specific claim

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3639191, Atypical IκB proteins – nuclear modulators of NF-κB signaling; PMCID:PMC5937028, Group 2 Innate Lymphoid Cells in Pulmonary Immunity and Tissue Homeostasis
primary_title: Interleukin-9 regulates NF-kappaB activity through BCL3 gene induction
decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows IL-9 transcriptionally upregulates BCL3 in T cells and mast cells through a JAK/STAT-associated response, with BCL3 expression altering p50 NF-κB activity and TNF-responsive transcription.
limitations_preserved: Preserve BCL3 as an IL-9-associated NF-kB-modulatory output and the T-cell/mast-cell context; do not infer direct terminal-TF status or transfer the TNF interaction to all IL-9 responses

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6028070, Negative Regulation of Cytokine Signaling in Immunity; PMCID:PMC3876435, SOCS3: An essential physiological inhibitor of signaling by interleukin-6 and G-CSF family cytokines
primary_title: Interleukin 9 induces expression of three cytokine signal inhibitors: cytokine-inducible SH2-containing protein, suppressor of cytokine signalling (SOCS)-2 and SOCS-3, but only SOCS-3 overexpression suppresses interleukin 9 signalling
decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows IL-9 rapidly induces CISH/CIS in BW5147 T-cell lymphoma cells and that IL-9-receptor/STAT pathway perturbations identify STAT1/3 and/or STAT5-dependent induction.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the rapid IL-9/STAT-associated gene induction and lymphoma/reconstitution context; CISH induction is a feedback output, while the primary found no suppression by CISH overexpression and no terminal-TF claim

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6028070, Negative Regulation of Cytokine Signaling in Immunity; PMCID:PMC3876435, SOCS3: An essential physiological inhibitor of signaling by interleukin-6 and G-CSF family cytokines
primary_title: Interleukin 9 induces expression of three cytokine signal inhibitors: cytokine-inducible SH2-containing protein, suppressor of cytokine signalling (SOCS)-2 and SOCS-3, but only SOCS-3 overexpression suppresses interleukin 9 signalling
decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows IL-9 rapidly induces SOCS2 in BW5147 T-cell lymphoma cells through STAT1/3 and/or STAT5-dependent receptor signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve SOCS2 as an IL-9-associated gene output rather than assuming it is the dominant IL-9 inhibitor; primary context is BW5147/reconstituted cells and not SCI-specific

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6028070, Negative Regulation of Cytokine Signaling in Immunity; PMCID:PMC3876435, SOCS3: An essential physiological inhibitor of signaling by interleukin-6 and G-CSF family cytokines
primary_title: Interleukin 9 induces expression of three cytokine signal inhibitors: cytokine-inducible SH2-containing protein, suppressor of cytokine signalling (SOCS)-2 and SOCS-3, but only SOCS-3 overexpression suppresses interleukin 9 signalling
decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows IL-9 induces SOCS3 in BW5147 T-cell lymphoma cells through STAT1/3-dependent signaling, and SOCS3 overexpression suppresses IL-9-induced STAT activation, gene induction and anti-apoptotic activity.
limitations_preserved: Preserve SOCS3 as the functionally inhibitory IL-9 feedback output and the BW5147/reconstituted-cell context; do not generalize to every IL-9 target or infer terminal-TF status
